funFact: Yogis have been sitting criss-cross like this for thousands of years!
story: A little explorer found the comfiest spot in the whole forest — a soft mossy cushion — and sat down criss-cross to watch the fireflies dance.
description: Sit down criss-cross applesauce! 🧘 Rest your hands on your knees like little starfish. Now grow your back tall, tall, TALL like a tower. Take a big slow breath — ahhh, easy peasy!

funFact: Danda means 'stick' in Sanskrit — this pose makes your spine straight as a wizard's staff!
story: The young wizard held their magic staff perfectly straight, and suddenly their whole body remembered how to sit as straight as the staff itself.
description: Sit with your legs stretched out in front like two long rulers! 📏 Press your palms into the floor beside you. Now sit up sooo straight — pretend a string is pulling the top of your head to the sky. Point your toes up and hold strong!

funFact: Butterflies taste with their feet — imagine tasting ice cream with your toes!
story: A brand-new butterfly sat on a flower, pressed its feet together, and slowly opened its beautiful wings for the very first time.
description: Sit down and press the bottoms of your feet together — smoosh! 🦋 Hold your feet like a little book. Let your knees float out to the sides like butterfly wings. Sit tall and feel your wings get ready to fly!

funFact: Some butterflies flap their wings up to 20 times every second!
story: The butterfly saw a garden full of flowers across the meadow, so it flapped its wings faster and faster and zoomed off on a nectar adventure.
description: Sit in butterfly with your feet pressed together! Now gently flap your knee-wings up and down — flap, flap, flap! 🦋 Can you flap slow like a sleepy butterfly? Now fast like a racing one? Wheee!

funFact: Vajra means 'thunderbolt' — you're sitting like a rock with thunder power inside!
story: High on a mountain sat a wise old rock. Storms blew and rivers rushed, but the rock stayed perfectly still and peaceful through it all.
description: Kneel down and sit back on your heels like a strong, still rock! 🪨 Rest your hands on your legs. Make your back tall and your body super still. Shhh... can you be as quiet as a mountain rock?

funFact: The tallest mountain on Earth, Mount Everest, grows a tiny bit taller every year — just like you!
story: A little hill dreamed of becoming a mighty mountain, so every morning it stretched its peak higher and higher toward the clouds.
description: Sit criss-cross and grow your back super tall! ⛰️ Now reach both arms way up high and press your palms together — you're the pointy top of a mountain! Stretch up, up, UP to the sky and hold strong.

benefits: Helps you squat like a pro
funFact: In many countries, people rest in this squat every day — it keeps hips happy for a whole lifetime!
story: A flower-picker squatted low in the garden, gathering blossom after blossom to string into a beautiful garland necklace.
description: Stand with your feet wide, then bend your knees and squat aaaall the way down! 🌺 Press your palms together in front of your heart. Use your elbows to gently push your knees wide. You're a little flower squatting in the garden!

funFact: Slow breathing sends a secret message to your brain that says 'everything is okay!'
story: On top of a misty mountain lived a tiny master who could sit so still and breathe so softly that hummingbirds landed right on their shoulders.
description: Sit criss-cross like a wise master on a mountaintop! 🧘 Rest your hands on your knees and make little circles with your fingers. Close your eyes softly. Breathe in slooowly... and out slooowly. You are calm. You are the master!

funFact: Long before books, people remembered whole stories by heart and told them around campfires!
story: Every evening the village gathered around the storyteller, who sat up tall, opened invisible pages, and made dragons and heroes come alive.
description: Sit criss-cross and hold your hands open like a big storybook! 📖 Sit up tall so everyone can hear you. Take a deep breath and whisper: 'Once upon a time...' What magical story will your body tell today?

funFact: Your heart is a drummer too — it beats about 100,000 times every single day!
story: The jungle band needed a drummer, so a little musician sat down criss-cross and drummed a beat so catchy that even the elephants started dancing.
description: Sit criss-cross with your hands on your knees — they're your drums! 🥁 Tap a slow beat... boom, boom, boom. Now speed it up — boomboomboom! Drum on your legs, then freeze! Can you drum super quietly too? Shhh-tap-tap.

funFact: Owls can turn their heads almost all the way around — about three-quarters of a full circle!
story: High in an old oak tree, a wise owl sat perfectly still, slowly turning its head to watch over all the sleeping forest friends.
description: Sit on your heels nice and tall — you're an owl on a branch! 🦉 Make big round owl eyes with your fingers. Slooowly turn your head to one side... then the other... What do you see? Give a soft 'hoo-hoo!'

funFact: A turtle's shell is part of its skeleton — it can never crawl out of it!
story: A shy little turtle heard a loud noise and tucked into its cozy shell. Inside it was warm and quiet, and soon the turtle felt brave again.
description: Sit with your knees bent wide and your feet on the floor. 🐢 Slowly duck your head down and slide your hands under your legs — you're hiding in your shell! Take a cozy breath in your quiet shell... then peek out. Hello, world!

funFact: Before clocks, people told time with shadows, sand, and even dripping water!
story: In a tidy little clock shop, the friendliest clock swayed its arms side to side — tick, tock — keeping perfect time for the whole town.
description: Sit criss-cross and reach your arms straight up — you're the clock's hands! 🕰️ Lean gently to one side and say 'tick!' Now lean to the other side — 'tock!' Keep your bottom glued to the floor. Tick... tock... what time is it?

funFact: Frogs don't drink water with their mouths — they soak it up through their skin!
story: The tiniest frog in the pond squatted low on a lily pad, staying very still and ready, watching a sparkly dragonfly zip by.
description: Squat down low with your feet wide — you're a tiny frog on a lily pad! 🐸 Put your hands on the floor between your feet. Stay low and still... ribbit, ribbit! Can you take three froggy breaths without hopping away?

funFact: Pressing your palms together at your heart is a friendly greeting used all around the world!
story: Two best friends met on a mountain path, pressed their palms together, and bowed — their secret way of saying 'my heart says hello to your heart.'
description: Sit criss-cross, nice and tall. Press your palms together right in front of your heart. 🙏 Close your eyes and breathe in something happy... breathe out a smile. Give a tiny bow — peace, friend!

benefits: Stretches one leg at a time
funFact: A butterfly resting with one wing out is soaking up sunshine to warm its flying muscles!
story: One butterfly wing got sleepy, so the butterfly stretched its other wing long across the grass and let the sun warm it up.
description: Sit with one leg stretched out long like a sunbeam. 🦋 Bend your other leg and press that foot to your straight leg's knee. Sit up tall — one wing folded, one wing long! Then switch sides so both wings get a turn.

funFact: Starfish can grow a whole new arm if they lose one — talk about super stretchy powers!
story: A little star fell gently from the sky, landed on the beach, and stretched its points out wide to say hello to the ocean.
description: Sit down and slide your legs out wide, wide, WIDE like a star! ⭐ Point your toes up to the sky. Press your hands on the floor in front of you and sit super tall. You're the brightest star on the beach!

funFact: Windshield wipers were invented back when cars still shared the road with horses!
story: Drip, drop — rain splashed on the little car's window, so its trusty wipers swished side to side until the road was clear for adventure.
description: Sit back on your hands with your knees bent and feet wide on the floor. 🚗 Now let both knees swish gently to one side... then swish to the other! Swish, swish, like wipers in the rain. Keep it slow and smooth!

funFact: Cats stretch their backs like this every time they wake up from a nap — up to 16 naps a day!
story: A sleepy cat and a happy cow were best friends who did their morning stretches together — arch and curl, moo and meow!
description: Sit criss-cross with your hands on your knees. Breathe in and puff your chest forward like a happy cow — moo! 🐱 Breathe out and round your back like a stretchy cat — meow! Go slow: moo... meow... moo... meow!

funFact: Each of your feet has 26 bones — that's about a quarter of all the bones in your body!
story: One morning a kid woke up and realized they'd never properly said good morning to their toes — so they reached down and greeted all ten, one by one.
description: Sit with your legs long in front of you. Wiggle your toes — hello, toes! 🦶 Now reach your hands toward your feet, walking your fingers down your legs. Give your toes a friendly wave or a gentle tickle. Good morning, little toes!

funFact: Vira means 'hero' in Sanskrit — real heroes know how to sit still and listen, too!
story: After saving the day, the young hero didn't need a trophy. They just knelt down tall and proud, ready for whatever adventure came next.
description: Kneel down with your knees together and your feet a little apart. 🦸 Sit your bottom down between your heels — or on a pillow if that feels better! Put your hands on your legs and lift your hero chest up tall. You're the hero of this story!

funFact: Pretzels were invented hundreds of years ago, and their twisty shape is said to look like folded arms!
story: At the silly bakery, one little pretzel decided it could twist itself into the fanciest shape of all — and won the golden salt sprinkle prize.
description: Sit criss-cross, then cross your legs extra snug! 🥨 Now give yourself a giant hug, wrapping your arms around your body. Squeeze gently — you're a warm, twisty pretzel fresh from the oven! Can you untangle without giggling?

benefits: Stretches the back of the leg
funFact: Janu means 'knee' and shirsha means 'head' — this pose's name tells you exactly what to do!
story: The sleepy moon leaned down over one long hill to whisper goodnight to it, then sat up to say goodnight to the other.
description: Sit with one leg long and the other foot tucked to your inner thigh. 🌙 Breathe in and reach your arms up tall. Breathe out and fold gently over your long leg, reaching for your foot. It's okay if you only reach your knee — hug what you can! Then switch legs.

funFact: Gymnasts and dancers practice this stretch to help them do splits and high kicks!
story: A kite spread its wings wide on the sand, then leaned forward into the breeze, dreaming of the moment it would soar.
description: Sit with your legs stretched out wide like a big letter V! 🪁 Point your toes up. Breathe in and grow tall... breathe out and walk your hands slowly forward on the floor. Go only as far as feels good — every little bit counts!

funFact: When butterflies rest, they fold up their wings and stay perfectly still — just like this pose!
story: After a whole day of flying, the butterfly folded softly over its feet, tucked in its wings, and listened to the garden hum.
description: Sit in butterfly with your feet pressed together. 🦋 Breathe in and sit up tall... breathe out and lean slooowly forward over your feet. Let your head hang heavy like a sleepy flower. Rest here and take three soft butterfly breaths.

funFact: Siddha means 'accomplished one' — ancient yogis called this the champion of sitting poses!
story: The star student of the mountain school learned the secret sitting position that made meditation feel as comfy as a cloud.
description: Sit tall and tuck one heel in close to your body. ✨ Now place your other foot gently in front of the first, like stacking two puzzle pieces. Rest your hands on your knees, palms up like little cups catching sunshine. Sit sparkly still!

funFact: Cows have best friends in their herd and get happier when they're together!
story: A clever cow wanted to scratch an itch right in the middle of its back, so it invented the fanciest arm stretch in the whole barnyard.
description: Sit tall and reach one arm way up high, then bend it so your hand pats your back. 🐮 Reach your other arm low and bend it up behind you. Try to make your fingers wave at each other — or hold a sock between them as a bridge! Switch arms after.

funFact: Baby deer can stand up and walk when they're only half an hour old!
story: A gentle deer settled into the tall meadow grass, folding its legs neatly to one side, ears up, listening to the forest's evening song.
description: Sit with both knees bent, then swing both feet to the same side so your legs make a zig-zag. 🦌 Sit up tall with proud deer posture. Perk up your ears — what do you hear? Then swing your legs to the other side.

funFact: Folding forward tells your body it's safe to slow down — that's why it feels so peaceful!
story: An autumn leaf floated down, down, down and folded softly over the ground, resting until the wind invited it to dance again.
description: Sit criss-cross and breathe in tall. 🍂 Now breathe out and walk your hands forward on the floor, folding gently over your legs. Let your head get heavy like a falling leaf. Rest and breathe... then slowly roll back up.

funFact: Strong, stretchy toes help you run faster, jump higher, and balance better!
story: The little rock climber discovered that the secret to climbing mountains wasn't big muscles — it was strong, bendy toes!
description: Kneel down, then tuck your toes under so they press into the floor. 🦶 Slowly sit back toward your heels — whoa, hello toes! It might feel big and stretchy, so breathe slow. Count to five, then release and wiggle your toes free!

funFact: Balancing wakes up a hidden sense in your ears that tells your brain which way is up!
story: The sneaky explorer needed to cross the creaky floor without a sound — so they squatted low on silent tiptoes like a shadow.
description: Squat down low, then lift your heels so you're balancing on your tiptoes! 🤸 Press your palms together at your heart. Wobble-wobble — that's your balance muscles working! If you tip over, giggle and try again.

funFact: Some say crossed legs in this pose look like a cow's face — the knees are the mouth and the feet are the ears!
story: Two cow friends sat down for a chat and stacked their knees just so — the comfiest gossip position in the whole pasture.
description: Sit down and cross one knee right on top of the other, like stacking pancakes! 🐮 Let your feet rest out to the sides. Sit up tall on both sitting bones. If your knees float up high, that's okay — they'll sink lower with practice. Switch sides!

funFact: Ducks waddle because their legs are set far back on their bodies — perfect for swimming!
story: Mama Duck led her ducklings across the farmyard in a wobbly waddling line — waddle, waddle, quack, quack — all the way to the pond.
description: Squat down low like a little duck! 🦆 Keep your bottom low and waddle forward — step, step, step! Flap your wing-elbows and say 'quack, quack!' Can you waddle in a circle without popping up? Waddle on, little duck!

funFact: Rocking side to side actually calms your brain — that's why babies love it!
story: The kind giant found a sleepy baby bird and cradled it ever so gently, rocking it side to side until it drifted off to dreamland.
description: Sit tall and lift one leg up, hugging it like a sleepy baby. 🍼 Cradle your foot in one elbow and your knee in the other. Now rock your leg-baby gently side to side... shhh, it's sleeping! Then softly switch legs.

funFact: Doves fold their wings neatly behind their backs when they rest — just like this pose!
story: The messenger dove had a secret: hidden behind its back, its wings folded together in a quiet hello that only other birds could see.
description: Sit criss-cross, nice and tall. 🕊️ Reach both arms behind your back and try to press your palms together like hidden praying hands. Too tricky? Just hold your elbows back there instead! Lift your chest and smile — you've got secret wings!

funFact: Your hip joint is a ball inside a socket — one of the bendiest joints in your whole body!
story: The numbers were playing hide and seek, and the number four hid the best — it disguised itself as a kid doing yoga!
description: Sit back on your hands with your knees bent and feet on the floor. 4️⃣ Now lift one foot and rest that ankle on your other knee — look, your legs make the number four! Sit tall and breathe. Feel the stretch in your hip? Switch legs!

funFact: Lotus flowers grow up from muddy water and open perfectly clean in the sunshine!
story: A lotus bud practiced opening one petal at a time. 'Half open is still beautiful,' said the sun — and it truly was.
description: Sit criss-cross, then gently lift one foot and rest it on top of your opposite thigh. 🪷 Keep your other leg folded underneath like usual. Sit tall and breathe like a blooming flower. Ease your foot down if anything pinches, and switch sides!
safetyNote: Never pull your foot into place — lift it gently, and come out right away if your knee complains.

funFact: Go means 'cow' and mukha means 'face' in Sanskrit — your folded legs make the cow's lips!
story: The champion stretcher of the barnyard could stack its legs AND clasp its hooves behind its back — all the other cows mooed in amazement.
description: Stack one knee on top of the other with your feet out to the sides. 🐮 Now reach one arm up and over your shoulder, and the other arm up behind your back. Try to hook your fingers together — or hold a sock between your hands! Sit tall and moo proudly. Switch sides!
safetyNote: Use a sock or strap between your hands instead of forcing them to touch. Skip the leg stack if your knees hurt.

funFact: Campers stack firewood in neat criss-cross layers so air can flow through — just like your legs in this pose!
story: The camping crew stacked their logs perfectly, shin on shin, and the campfire that night glowed brighter than all the stars.
description: Sit tall and bend both knees. 🔥 Stack one shin right on top of the other, like two logs for a campfire — ankle over knee, knee over ankle. Flex your feet strong! If your top knee sticks way up, slide a pillow under it. Breathe warm, cozy breaths.
safetyNote: If your knees hurt, keep the top leg in easy criss-cross instead of stacking. Never press down on your knee.

funFact: Your side body has breathing muscles between every rib — this stretch helps them all open up!
story: The painter leaned way over sideways to paint a rainbow across the whole sky, stretching their brush from the ground all the way up to the sun.
description: Sit with one leg stretched out wide and your other foot tucked in. 🌈 Lean sideways over your long leg, sliding your same-side arm down your shin. Now sweep your top arm up and over your ear — you're painting a giant rainbow! Breathe into your stretchy side, then switch.
safetyNote: Lean sideways, not forward, and only as far as feels comfy. Come up slowly if you feel dizzy.

funFact: Marichi was a legendary sage whose name means 'ray of light'!
story: The sage Ray-of-Light had a trick for catching sunbeams: wrap one arm around a knee, fold forward, and hold on tight until the light filled you up.
description: Sit with one leg long and the other knee bent up tall, foot flat on the floor. 🧙 Wrap your arm around your bent knee and hug it close. Breathe in tall... breathe out and fold gently over your long leg. You caught the sunbeam! Switch sides.
safetyNote: Keep the hug gentle and your back long — fold only as far as feels good.

funFact: This pose's name means 'bow up to the ear' — archers pull their bowstring right back to their ear before they shoot!
story: The forest archer took aim at a faraway apple, pulled the bowstring back to their ear, breathed out slowly... and — twang! — hit it right in the middle.
description: Sit with your legs long and grab one big toe with each hand — or hold your ankles! 🏹 Keep holding your straight leg's foot, and pull your other foot up toward your ear like a bowstring. Squint one eye, take aim... and gently lower. Twang! Switch sides, archer!
safetyNote: Pull your foot up slowly and stop if your hip or knee pinches. Bending the bottom leg is totally fine.

benefits: Deeply stretches the back of the leg
funFact: Herons can stand perfectly still for many minutes waiting for a fish — champion patience!
story: At the misty pond, a heron lifted one long leg straight up like a periscope, watching silently for the flash of a silver fish.
description: Sit tall with one leg folded back beside you or bent in close. 🪶 Hold your other foot with both hands and slooowly stretch that leg up toward the sky. Keep your back tall like a proud heron! A bent knee is perfectly fine. Lower gently and switch legs.
safetyNote: Keep a soft bend in the lifted knee and sit on a cushion if folding your leg back feels uncomfortable.

funFact: The lotus is one of the most famous yoga poses in the world — ancient statues thousands of years old show yogis sitting exactly like this!
story: In the middle of the quiet pond, the great lotus finally opened all its petals at once, and the whole pond glowed pink in the morning light.
description: Sit tall and gently lift one foot onto your opposite thigh, then the other foot on top of the other thigh. 🪷 Both feet rest like petals! Place your hands on your knees, palms up. Sit as still as a flower on quiet water. If it's too much, half lotus is just as lovely!
safetyNote: Only with a grown-up watching, and only if your hips are very open. Stop right away if your knees or ankles feel any pinch — half lotus or criss-cross is always a great choice.

funFact: Some tortoises live longer than 150 years — slow and steady really does win!
story: The oldest, wisest turtle in the sea tucked its flippers under its shell, sank into the soft sand, and dreamed of the days when the ocean was young.
description: Sit with your legs wide and your knees bent a little. 🐢 Fold forward slooowly and slide your arms under your knees, reaching out to the sides. Let your chest sink low like a turtle tucking into its shell. Breathe slow, sleepy turtle breaths... then carefully wiggle your arms free.
safetyNote: Only with a grown-up spotter. Keep your knees bent, move super slowly, and come out right away if your back or legs feel strained.
